mechanism_narrative: When monthly GDP components (GDPC1) show a two-month consecutive increase exceeding 3%, it indicates accelerating demand, which is associated with a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases for two consecutive months by more than 3%
failure_condition: In a contractionary regime as defined by UNRATE < 4% and FEDFUNDS > 5%, the 20-day forward return is non-positive.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the CPIAUCSL inflation index above 0.5% in a month triggers a preemptive rate hike expectation, which negatively impacts short-term equity valuations and produces a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases by more than 0.5% in a single month
failure_condition: No significant negative return occurs when inflation exceeds 0.5% in a month and FEDFUNDS remains unchanged for two subsequent months.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly increases in employment (PAYEMS) of at least 2% for three months signals labor market strength that supports corporate earnings growth, driving a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by at least 2% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: During a recession regime (UNRATE > 6.5% and INDPRO < 50), the 20-day forward return is not statistically positive.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below 0.5% for two months suggests supply-side weakness, which reduces growth expectations and yields a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by more than 0.5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: When INDPRO remains above 50 (2017=100) for the preceding 6 months, the signal is neutral and no return bias is observed.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous strength in both consumer demand (HOUST) and business demand (RSAFS) above their 12-month moving averages creates a dual-up signal that increases investor confidence and produces a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: Both HOUST and RSAFS exceed their respective 12-month moving averages
failure_condition: If either HOUST or RSAFS falls below its 12-month moving average within the 60-day window, the return is non-positive.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% for three months indicates a tightening labor market, prompting the Fed to hold rates steady but signal future hikes, which results in a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: When UNRATE remains above 4% for the next 6 months, the forward return is not significantly negative.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in monthly payroll growth (PAYEMS) by more than 5% suggests softening labor demand, which depresses earnings expectations and produces a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS decreases by more than 5% in a single month
failure_condition: If PAYEMS increases by >2% in the following month, the negative return signal reverses.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS rising and UNRATE falling), the S&P 500 exhibits a negative 20-day forward return regardless of other macro variables, indicating risk aversion to future rate hikes.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases and UNRATE decreases over the preceding month
failure_condition: In a non-tightening regime (FEDFUNDS flat and UNRATE rising), the 20-day forward return is not significantly negative.
